newsitem.title: USA: Kansas unveils $1.5 bln interim roads plan.
newsitem.headline: Kansas unveils $1.5 bln interim roads plan.

text.p: Kansas transportation officials unveiled a $1.5 billion interim road funding plan for the next four years made possible by favorable bond sales.

Lower-than-expected interest rates on highway bonds sold for a just-concluded eight-year transportation department made it possible to reconstruct 200 more miles of non-interstate roads over the next four years, the department announced Friday.
Federal aid also exceeded expectations and low inflation reduced anticipated construction costs for the comprehensive highway program that concluded in fiscal 1997, the department said.

Kansas had projected no highway projects after fiscal 1997 when officials announced the comprehensive program, the department noted. The transportation department had rebuilt an average of 205 miles of roads per year under that program.
Funding constraints have limited the interim plan and even that limited amount cannot be sustained for an extended period without new funding legislation, the department said.
